selectedDecisions.title: Initial versus routine scan
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep 30 calendar days only for the one-time initial catch-up. Routine runs resume from the last completed discovery checkpoint and cover the entire missed interval.

selectedDecisions.title: Published stop losses
selectedDecisions.decision: Mirror Bravos's latest published stop-loss price and explicit changes for each position. Include it in entry proposals and verify the actual copied position's setting. Do not mark an accepted update as applied until broker read-back confirms it.

selectedDecisions.title: Entry ceiling for future alerts
selectedDecisions.decision: Explicitly apply the no-chasing rule to future opening alerts as well: compare the actual buy ask with that opening alert's published entry. A price above the ceiling fails the entry check; do not add an unapproved tolerance.

selectedDecisions.title: Re-entry after a stop executes
selectedDecisions.decision: After a verified stop exit, close our position cycle and do not reopen from its old opening or a later addition to that old cycle. Require a new explicit Bravos opening; ambiguous re-entry language goes to review.

selectedDecisions.title: Missing or incompatible stop
selectedDecisions.decision: Do not propose an unprotected new entry. If the published stop is missing, ambiguous or broker-incompatible, block that entry and report the exact issue. For an existing holding, preserve its current protection while the discrepancy is resolved; never silently clear it.

selectedDecisions.title: What belongs in Git
selectedDecisions.decision: Version a minimal alert/decision ledger and run reports in this local Git repo. Keep secrets and raw account responses ignored; exclude unnecessary personal identifiers. Keep it local until you explicitly request a remote or backup destination.

selectedDecisions.title: Basis for percentage weights
selectedDecisions.decision: Size each new opening from the current real equity of this Bravos allocation at evaluation time, using its Bravos weight. Cap spending by available cash after pending commitments and costs. Funding changes alone never resize existing positions.

selectedDecisions.title: How to apply reductions
selectedDecisions.decision: Apply the proportional reduction to our linked units: a Bravos change from 5 to 4 sells 20% of those units. A full close closes all linked remaining units. Do not rebalance to a current-equity target.

selectedDecisions.title: How to apply additions
selectedDecisions.decision: For an existing linked holding, add the increase in Bravos weight times current real Bravos equity. Use the addition alert's published price as that addition's ceiling. Apply the entry evaluation and expiry rules to that event; never resize the old units merely to restore a target weight.

selectedDecisions.title: Initial catch-up after weight changes
selectedDecisions.decision: For initial catch-up, use the latest still-open Bravos weight, the original opening price ceiling and the latest published stop. Do not replay historical buys, additions and trims. Thus CF would use 4%, subject to all other checks.

selectedDecisions.title: Multiple take-profit targets
selectedDecisions.decision: Use Bravos's stated quantities at each target when provided. Do not assume equal thirds. If only prices are given, retain all targets and wait for explicit profit-taking/reduction instructions; research their published allocation convention first.

selectedDecisions.title: Entry already at or beyond the stop
selectedDecisions.decision: For a long opening, reject a catch-up entry at or below its latest published stop. Do not move the stop to make the trade fit. Require a fresh Bravos setup or an explicit clarification before reconsidering that cycle.

selectedDecisions.title: Order type and entry-price enforcement
selectedDecisions.decision: Require a broker-supported entry method that demonstrably enforces the chosen price ceiling. If eToro Agent Portfolios cannot provide that guarantee, report the incompatibility; do not silently use a market or market-if-touched order as an equivalent. Later execution must reconcile partial fills and cancel any remaining entry quantity at expiry.

selectedDecisions.title: Run times, quote age and expiry
selectedDecisions.decision: Propose two runs at 10:00 and 15:30 America/New_York on US trading days, with timezone conversion handling daylight saving. Evaluate entries only while their exchange is open, using asks no older than 60 seconds. Routine entry/add intents expire at the close of their first evaluated trading session; catch-up uses its separately chosen activation session. Do not schedule anything yet.

selectedDecisions.title: Insufficient cash and minimum orders
selectedDecisions.decision: Use source publication order for new entries/additions, with a stable ID tie-break for equal dates. Keep the specified size: never round up or redistribute skipped weights. If cash or minimums prevent that size, skip that event and report why. Reconcile exit proceeds before treating them as available.

selectedDecisions.title: Enforce state integrity
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep strategy logic in precise English, but use small deterministic helpers for exclusive locking, schema/ID validation, hashing and atomic ledger commits. Test them with local fixtures. Do not build a trading executor as part of this item.

selectedDecisions.title: Priority of operations
selectedDecisions.decision: After reconciliation, handle full exits and reductions first, then stop discrepancies/updates for remaining positions, then additions and new openings. Respect source chronology within a cycle. Record linked actions as one plan so a stop change is not lost inside a trim.

selectedDecisions.title: Backdated articles and discovery limits
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep incremental discovery plus dashboard reconciliation. On a mismatch, expand the targeted history until explained and block only affected proposals. Record the coverage boundary honestly; do not claim full historical detection without a publisher change feed or full archive inventory.

selectedDecisions.title: Weekly review of old resolved articles
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep a once-per-week revision check of known resolved alert URLs, distinct from discovering new alerts. Record it as source maintenance; do not revive old trades. If it becomes costly, revise the cadence explicitly rather than silently dropping coverage.

selectedDecisions.title: Reread active and unresolved articles
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep this check each run while those cycles are active or unresolved. Read article revisions for changed stops or instructions; deduplicate unchanged content and exclude subscriber comments.

selectedDecisions.title: Archive changes while scanning
selectedDecisions.decision: Recheck the first page after traversal. If IDs changed, merge and repeat once. If it changes again, save partial evidence and report incomplete discovery without advancing the checkpoint. Do not loop indefinitely.

selectedDecisions.title: JSON ledger and history
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep a schema-versioned JSON ledger as authoritative memory and Markdown run reports for reading. Retain immutable prior ledger versions and record which rules produced each decision. Apply the Git/privacy choice separately; a local Git repo is not an off-device backup.

selectedDecisions.title: Content fingerprints
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep both: normalize only whitespace/line endings, exclude page chrome and comments, hash the Bravos-authored body, and compare material trade facts. Preserve revisions; never turn an edited article into a second opening solely because its hash changed.

selectedDecisions.title: Locking and interrupted-run recovery
selectedDecisions.decision: Keep one writer at a time, validate and atomically replace the ledger, and preserve the prior version. Recover a stale claim only after establishing its owner stopped. Check the committed generation and broker state before retrying any uncertain work.
